rubric.note: Subjective internal editorial ratings with evidence; not an automatic humour metric or an independent live review.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hide this envelope under the picnic hamper before anyone comes in.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What's in it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Something easier to explain once it isn't visible.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Am I involved now?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only at the hamper level. We can discuss promotion later.

card.title: Help Me Keep This Quiet
card.instruction: Get someone to help contain a secret without first revealing its full risk or purpose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep this cupboard key until tomorrow and don't mention the cupboard.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because a cupboard with a secret key attracts questions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've made me curious.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Keep the curiosity in your pocket with the key.

card.title: Help Me Keep This Quiet
card.instruction: Get someone to help contain a secret without first revealing its full risk or purpose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you catch your bus, explain the missing hour on this receipt.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can talk tomorrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The bus leaves in ten minutes. The hour's already gone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I took a detour.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then give the detour a destination before yours begins.

card.title: Not Until You Explain
card.instruction: Keep someone present until they account for one contradiction, omission, or suspicious change in their story.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wait. This note used to say Friday. Why does it say Monday?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I have to leave.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not until Monday explains what it did to Friday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I changed the booking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Now explain why my name stayed on it.

card.title: Not Until You Explain
card.instruction: Keep someone present until they account for one contradiction, omission, or suspicious change in their story.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm not asking you to apologise for cancelling. Apologise for not telling me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I didn't want to upset you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So you let me arrive with a cake instead.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry the party didn't happen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Try the part where I didn't know.

card.title: Apologize for the Lie
card.instruction: Make someone acknowledge that the concealment or misdirection mattered, even if the underlying choice was defensible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You gave me half the letter. That changed my answer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You got the important facts.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You kept the fact that would have made me say no.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought I was helping.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then acknowledge what your help prevented me from choosing.

card.title: Apologize for the Lie
card.instruction: Make someone acknowledge that the concealment or misdirection mattered, even if the underlying choice was defensible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We were collecting chairs, not investigating the locked cupboard. Agreed?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We did open the cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Between chairs. Let's emphasise the furniture.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What if they ask about the key?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can agree it was a very practical chair-collecting tool.

card.title: Approve the Cover Story
card.instruction: Get someone to endorse an explanation that protects the plan, reputation, or people involved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Back my explanation that the missing hour was traffic.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We were parked.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stationary traffic. Very slow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Outside the bakery?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. A known bottleneck near cakes.

card.title: Approve the Cover Story
card.instruction: Get someone to endorse an explanation that protects the plan, reputation, or people involved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep this labelled box in your cupboard. I'll handle the calls.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your name's on the label.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Mine is the first cupboard they'll check.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're making me responsible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For storage. Let's keep the job description reassuringly narrow.

card.title: You Handle the Evidence
card.instruction: Make someone else take responsibility for the evidence, loose end, or difficult follow-up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You explain the missing receipt to the treasurer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's your receipt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's why my voice sounds so personally involved.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What should I say?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start with administrative confusion. You sound neutral saying it.

card.title: You Handle the Evidence
card.instruction: Make someone else take responsibility for the evidence, loose end, or difficult follow-up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Was the parcel in a bag or a box? You've used both words.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A bag, I think.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Describe the handles before choosing the noun.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It had a rigid lid.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Let's build the object before the story.

card.title: What Really Happened?
card.instruction: Find the truth by comparing details, repeating questions, and testing which parts of the story remain consistent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell me again what happened between four and four-ten.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already explained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it should match one of these two versions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I stopped for coffee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Where does coffee fit into the version with the bus?

card.title: What Really Happened?
card.instruction: Find the truth by comparing details, repeating questions, and testing which parts of the story remain consistent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When they ask, we arrived after the lights went out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I arrived before.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you were early for our agreed account.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I won't say something false.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you say you remember it being dark eventually?

card.title: Back My Version
card.instruction: Recruit someone to remember, repeat, and defend one shared version of events when questions begin.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Repeat this: the extra key was for maintenance.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It opened the cake cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A cupboard needs maintaining.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Does eating cake count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not in the version I'd like you to defend.

card.title: Back My Version
card.instruction: Recruit someone to remember, repeat, and defend one shared version of events when questions begin.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Try this explanation on the chair before I sign it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why don't you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I need an independent reading of the room.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's in your handwriting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Read it aloud. We're testing the explanation, not the pen.

card.title: Test the Story First
card.instruction: Get someone else to repeat the explanation, ask the dangerous question, or test the risky step before you commit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask why the account's empty. I'll listen from here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Come with me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I will if the answer sounds welcoming.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's not support.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It's advance research for the support stage.

card.title: Test the Story First
card.instruction: Get someone else to repeat the explanation, ask the dangerous question, or test the risky step before you commit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before calling it our discovery, mention who found the receipt.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We all solved the problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. After my receipt introduced it properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll put your name in the report.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Beside found, not beside attended.

card.title: Credit for the Discovery
card.instruction: Make someone acknowledge that you found the clue, saw through the deception, or designed the successful scheme.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My diagram located the hidden doorway.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We all studied the wall.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I drew a door while it was still a wall to everyone else.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Thank you for helping.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Discovering. A more accurate verb for the diagram.

card.title: Credit for the Discovery
card.instruction: Make someone acknowledge that you found the clue, saw through the deception, or designed the successful scheme.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That question's answer is in this letter. Our promise is beside it. Which do you pick up?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They deserve the truth.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then name what happens to our confidence when you hand it over.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're making me choose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The question already did. I'm making the choice visible.

card.title: Truth or Loyalty
card.instruction: Make someone choose between protecting the relationship and answering a dangerous question honestly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will you tell them where we were, or keep our agreement?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't I do both?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not with the address included.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't want to lie.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then decide what part of us you're willing to explain.

card.title: Truth or Loyalty
card.instruction: Make someone choose between protecting the relationship and answering a dangerous question honestly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Was the missing cake taken, dropped, or eaten by the dog? Describe the crumbs before choosing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's icing on the dog.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dog leads. Were those crumbs present before dinner too?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes, after you fed it your slice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then theft returns to contention. Start again with who opened the cupboard.

bespokePairs.seedUse: Competing explanations guide exact evidence questions; new details force A to shift theory rather than stack unconnected accusations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The parcel was lost, stolen, or delivered elsewhere. Was it a bag or a box?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A box with handles.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Delivery error leads. Describe the lid.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was tied, not hinged.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then 'box' loses support. Let's establish the container before accusing a driver.

bespokePairs.seedUse: Adapts S144-single-b's competing explanations and changing preference to a missing parcel, using D126-single-a's bag-versus-box, handles and lid inquiry. A1 proposes loss, theft and misdelivery; A3 favors delivery error after B2 describes handles, while A5 uses B4's tied lid to reconsider the container label. The last change concerns classification, not a demonstrated switch among the original disappearance theories. That exact-pair fidelity reservation remains pending; this amendment corrects source attribution without approving the dialogue.

card.title: Competing Theories
card.instruction: Create several explanations for what is happening. Test each new clue against them, and switch allegiance whenever one theory gains strength.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our wedding cake's gone: theft, accident, or the dog. I suspect theft.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's icing on him. Get him outside before Mum sees.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dog leads. I'll take him; check under the table for crumbs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That icing's from yesterday. The crumbs lead into the cloakroom.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Theft leads again. Keep the dog here; let's see whether that trail ends at a dropped cake or somebody's coat.

card.instruction: Find the truth by comparing details, repeating questions, and testing which parts of the story remain consistent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Was the parcel in a bag or a box? You've used both words.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A bag, I think.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Describe the handles before choosing the noun.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It had a rigid lid.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Let's build the object before the story.

card.title: Competing Theories
card.instruction: Create several explanations for what is happening. Test each new clue against them, and switch allegiance whenever one theory gains strength.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The hall lights failed: weather, wiring, or the caretaker saving electricity. Wiring's my favourite.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He unplugged them. Help me reach the socket.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Economy takes the lead. I'll hold your ladder.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The socket's wet. There's rain coming through the roof.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Weather overtakes him. Leave the plug; let's ask whether he unplugged it before the leak.
